claim_summary: TRACE combines DER-specific CoT instruction fine-tuning with multi-agent feedback refinement and factuality-checked summaries for time-series forecasting, and evaluates the framework on imputation.

claim_evidence.quote: An instruction fine-tuning method based on CoT reasoning is designed to address the unique characteristics of DERs time series. Through chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, the prior knowledge embedded in pretrained LLMs is traced and aligned with the requirements of DERs power time series forecasting tasks.
In this context, this article proposes MaC framework designed to implement a thought refinement and correction process for LLMs through cooperative reasoning.

modules.name: DER-specific CoT instruction fine-tuning
modules.scope_reason: R2 places instruction fine-tuning that shapes model reasoning on the LLM side; it changes model behavior through training rather than only surrounding execution.
rubric_path: R2:LLM - instruction fine-tuning shapes model reasoning

evidence.quote: An instruction fine-tuning method based on CoT reasoning is designed to address the unique characteristics of DERs time series.
no additional retraining was performed on LLMs with accessible data, only instruction fine-tuning was applied.

modules.name: DER-specific CoT relevance selection
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 applies because the selector chooses reasoning steps by their contribution to the given forecasting task; changing to a different task objective requires redesigning the selected reasoning criteria. It is not GTS because its core input is the task objective and CoT relevance, rather than temporal state or information availability by themselves.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - selector is explicitly for the task objective

evidence.quote: For a given task, only a limited subset of CoT processes may be relevant. Therefore, the specific CoT elements required for a given task are determined by a relevance selector
imputation capability. No modifications were made to the CoT or MaC structures, only “task description” was altered (e.g., “...please impute the missing data”).

modules.name: Multi-agent forecast feedback refinement
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 applies because predictors revise numerical forecasts from summaries of other agents' predictions and the Judge outputs a final prediction; another task objective changes what agents predict and what the Judge aggregates. It is not GTS because this is not a task-independent temporal data management or validation mechanism.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - feedback and final output are tied to forecasting

evidence.quote: These summaries are then fed back to the respective predictor agents, allowing each agent to observe the statistical mean of the other agents’ predictions. Based on this feedback, each agent refines its predictions and generates a new output.
imputation capability. No modifications were made to the CoT or MaC structures, only “task description” was altered (e.g., “...please impute the missing data”).

modules.name: Judge-summary factuality verification
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 does not apply: the check scores whether a Judge summary is supported by agents' reasoning, rather than embedding a forecasting objective or task-family output criterion. R3_2 does not apply because it does not check chronology or temporal information availability. R3_3 applies as an execution verification checkpoint; the same summary-grounding check is used when the task description changes.
rubric_path: R2:Harness - summary verification around model calls
R3_2_GTS:no - no temporal-order or availability check

evidence.quote: In the MaC framework, we further integrated a Factuality Verification module. Following the methodology proposed by Feng et al. [27], a scoring metric Scorefact was introduced to assess the factual accuracy of the generated summaries
We consider three metrics: lexical overlap, semantic consistency, and factual consistency

task_performance.quote: The imputation MAE for all models is presented in Table V, all results are averaged over missing ratio of 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20%. As shown, TRACE achieves SOTA imputation performance due to its exceptional FSL capabilities.

notes: The paper explicitly reuses the unchanged CoT and MaC structures for imputation by altering the task description. The evaluation reports task errors and dataset-contamination checks, but no temporal split or information-availability validation.
